column1: # The seat grammar's shared case table (app#480, ADR-0034 D2).
# A seat is the workspace / participant name (the `<seat>` in
# grammar has ONE Go definition, identity.SeatPattern; every other
# implementation of it is a copy that this table holds equal:
#   - shell: charts/ctf-user/deploy-user.sh (its SEAT_PATTERN), run row by row
#            scripts/preflight-identity.sh read the SAME rows (their PR is the
#            paired one; until it lands they are not checked against this file).
# A row is never dropped to make an implementation pass: the implementation
# that disagrees is the bug. A change to the grammar changes the rows in the
#   - blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored
#   - split each line on its FIRST tab only. `input` may be empty (the line then
#     starts with a tab) and contains neither a tab nor a newline literally
#   - do NOT read it with `IFS=$'\t' read` (a tab is IFS whitespace there, so an
#   - characters that cannot be written literally are placeholders, decoded by
#     letter); the file itself stays ASCII
# Rows marked (B) are the ones whose verdict changes when the grammar is
# tightened to the set a workspace can actually be deployed with (1..53
# characters, ending in a letter or digit: app#480); they pin today's verdict.
# --- baseline: what the roster actually holds
# --- length (B): today up to 63 characters; Helm accepts a release name of at most 53
# --- a trailing '-' (B): accepted today; a Helm release name must end in a letter or digit
# --- control and bidi characters ({LF}: a trailing newline is not accepted; $ is not a line anchor here)
